course_name_en: Mechanics, Construction and Design of Structures

learning_outcomes.text: Familiarize students with the basic principles of air quality protection and its evaluation methods, then with the possibilities of reducing pollutant emission concentrations so that the immission level falls within legislatively permitted limits; technical applications are intended to concretely explain and interpret general and specific concepts regarding processes within energy recovery systems.
Understand standardized monitoring methods for pollution generated by combustion installations, operating on fossil or renewable (bio-fuels) fuels.

Understand the need for air quality protection, highlighting aspects related to reducing greenhouse gas emissions at the installation and global level, according to recent international decisions, to reduce the increase in average annual temperature by less than 2 degrees (1.5 degrees) compared to the 1990 level.

Familiarize with the calculation, data analysis, and correct interpretation of numerical results related to air pollution and its reduction measures, given that it is associated with industrial and domestic activities, as well as transport, activities/domains that are inextricably linked to the concept of civilization and evolution of human society, comfort in industry, transport, and generally in the national economy.
Understand and know investigation techniques according to national and European legislation.

syllabus_topics: General notions about air composition and quality. Pollutants. Combustion sources. Legislation. Role of the environmental expert/manager in an economic unit.
Harmful effect of pollutants: CO, NOx, SO2, VOC, ozone, particles.
Measurement of emission concentrations (CO, CO2, NOx, SO2, particles) with a station.
Measurement of pollutant emissions with a portable device - TESTO mobile system.
Measurement of flow rates, mass and volumetric concentrations with different systems.

Measurement of immissions, especially NOx, SO2, ozone, PM, VOC - demonstration and practical online monitoring campaign. Based on internally developed calculation programs, air quality management/environmental balance and pollutant dispersion simulations are also possible.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated from a 66% component for course activities (including flash tests, written exam, homework) and a 34% component for applied activities (including tests and oral examinations). To pass the course, the final grade must be a minimum of 5. Additionally, both the examination grade and the overall laboratory grade must be a minimum of 5.
